title: Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
key_facts: Nikon says the first-place video in its Small World in Motion contest, by Dr. Ning Xu, 'did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI'.
The BBC reports the video claimed to show cilia, tiny hair-like structures, moving in the airway of a child with the respiratory condition PCD.
Nikon began reviewing it last week after online scepticism.
Dr. Xu said on LinkedIn that an unsupervised neural-network method was used for AI-assisted post-processing of super-resolution optical images.
The video was disqualified and apparently removed; Nguyen Nam Nhat's video now holds first place.
Nikon will revisit its rules and evaluation procedures and says the decision is not a judgment of Xu's reputation, contributions or intent.
quote_evidence: Nikon says the video that originally won first place "did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI."
Nikon says it plans to "revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries."
why_it_matters_hint: Shows contests struggling to police AI-processed science imagery.
event_date: Disqualification reported 9 Oct 2026; review began the week before
notes: The Verge relays BBC reporting and Nikon's statement; Xu's LinkedIn comment quoted by The Verge.
